Rashi on Arakhin 29a:10:1.hebrew: רב גמריה גמיר - מרביה, דרביה אגמריה דמתני' משבשתא היא:
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:10:1.english: Rav learned his tradition - from his teacher, for his teacher taught him that the Mishnah is erroneous:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:11:1.hebrew: ושדינהו - לד' זוזי בנהרא, דהקדש הן לבדק הבית; דאי לכהן, לית להו פדיון, ולכהן בעי מיתבינהו:
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:11:1.english: And throw them - [meaning] the four zuzim into the river, for they are consecrated property [designated] for Temple maintenance; for if [they were] for a priest, they would have no redemption, and he would have to give them to a priest:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:13:1.hebrew: בזמן הזה - דליכא בית וליכא פסידא, אלא איסורא הוא דרביעא עלייהו, אפילו לכתחלה נמי:
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:13:1.english: In the present time - Since there is no Temple and there is no loss [to the Temple treasury], rather it is [only] a prohibition that rests upon them [the consecrated items], [one may desacralize them] even ab initio as well:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:15:1.english: [The law of] a Hebrew slave is not practiced - [meaning] that he is not sold in the present era:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:16:1.hebrew: ואין שדה אחוזה - לא נהג דין שדה אחוזה שתהא נגאלת בגירוע, אלא אם ירצה הלוקח להחזירה לו בדמים שירצה מחזיר, ואם לאו אין כופין אותו. וכן דין מקדיש שדה אחוזה בזמן הבית ואין היובל נוהג — כגון משגלו שבט ראובן וגד שבטלו היובלות — אין נגאלת אלא בשויה:
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:16:1.english: And [the law of] an ancestral field does not [apply] - The law of an ancestral field, that it be redeemed with a deduction [for the years remaining until the Jubilee, does not apply]; rather, if the buyer wishes to return it to him for whatever price he wishes, he returns [it], and if not, we do not compel him. And likewise, [regarding] the law of one who consecrates an ancestral field when the Temple [is standing] and the Jubilee is not observed — for example, from when the tribe[s] of Reuben and Gad were exiled, when the Jubilees ceased — it is only redeemed at its [full] value:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:16:2.hebrew: אין בתי ערי חומה נוהגין - דלא כייפינן ליה ללוקח, אם בא מוכר לגאלה, אפילו בתוך שנה:
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:16:2.english: [The laws of] houses of walled cities do not apply - [meaning] that we do not compel the buyer [to return it] if the seller comes to redeem it, even within a year:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:17:1.english: [The law of] a resident alien [ger toshav] does not apply - [i.e., the obligation] that a Jew is commanded to sustain him. A ger toshav [is a gentile] who accepted upon himself not to worship idols, while eating unslaughtered meat [neveilot]:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:18:1.hebrew: כתיב - בעבד עברי "כי טוב לו עמך", וכתיב בגר תושב "עמך ישב וגו'", ד"לא תסגיר עבד אל אדוניו" בגר תושב משתעי, דהכי מוקמינן לה במסכת גיטין בפ' השולח גט (דף מה.), וכתיב בתריה "עמך ישב בקרבך וגו'": מכל מקום לתרוייהו קשיא, דקתני "אין שדה חרמים נוהג אלא בזמן יובל":
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:18:1.english: It is written - regarding a Hebrew slave, "because he fares well with you," and it is written regarding a resident alien [ger toshav], "he shall dwell with you, etc." — for [the verse] "You shall not hand over a slave to his master" speaks of a resident alien, as we establish it thus in Tractate Gittin in the chapter [entitled] HaSholeiach Get (45a), and it is written after it: "He shall dwell with you in your midst, etc." In any case, [this baraita] poses a difficulty for both of them, as it teaches: "[The law of] a dedicated field applies only at a time when the Jubilee [is observed]":

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:19:1.hebrew: מקרקעי - אין נוהגין בהן חרמין, כדכתיב "בצאתו ביובל כשדה החרם":
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:19:1.english: Land - [dedications (charamim)] do not apply [to it], as it is written: "when it goes out in the Jubilee, as a devoted field":

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:1:1.english: They are like consecrated [property] - and [the prohibition of] misuse of consecrated property [me'ilah] applies to them:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:1:2.english: They are like non-sacred [property] - like the rest of the priest's property:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:20:1.hebrew: כתוב אחד אומר תקדיש - גבי בכור, דכתיב: "כל הבכור [וגו'] תקדיש" (דברים טו):
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:20:1.english: One verse states: “You shall consecrate” - Regarding a firstborn [animal], as it is written: “All the firstborn [etc.] you shall consecrate” (Deuteronomy 15[:19]):

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:20:2.english: And one verse states: “[A man] shall not consecrate [it]” - “However, the firstborn among animals that is born first to the Lord, a man shall not consecrate it,” etc. (Leviticus 27:26):

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:21:1.hebrew: הקדש עילוי - להעלותו בדמים, ויתן טובת הנאתו לכהן:
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:21:1.english: A consecration of value - [meaning] to elevate it in value [by consecrating its monetary worth], and he gives its benefit of discretion to a priest.

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:21:2.english: And you cannot consecrate it [by] a consecration for the altar - [meaning] that the designation of another sacrifice should take effect upon it:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:22:1.english: And the Rabbis - who derive this exposition (above, Arakhin 28b) from [the verse], “Every dedicated item is most sacred”:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:22:2.hebrew: אל תקדיש מיבעי ליה ללאו - שאם מתפיסו לשם זבח אחר, עובר בלאו:
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:22:2.english: "Shall not consecrate" is necessary for a negative commandment - that if one designates it [the firstborn] for the sake of another offering, he transgresses a negative commandment:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:22:3.hebrew: שמצוה להקדישו - לשם בכור, ואף על פי שהוא קדוש מאליו:
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:22:3.english: That it is a mitzvah to consecrate it - as a firstborn [offering], even though it is [already] sanctified on its own:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:23:1.hebrew: ורבי ישמעאל - אמר לך: "אי לא מקדיש ליה לא קדיש?" — בתמיה:
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:23:1.english: And Rabbi Yishmael - would say to you: "If one does not consecrate it, is it [therefore] not consecrated?" — [this is said] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:23:2.english: He does not need to consecrate it - And Rabbi Yishmael does not accept this exposition:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:2:1.hebrew: בשלמא רבנן - דמתניתין מפרשי טעמא וקרא דרבי יהודה, כדקתני: א"כ למה נאמר כל חרם כו':
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:2:1.english: Granted, the Rabbis - [the Rabbis] of the Mishnah explain [their] reason and Rabbi Yehuda [ben Beteira]'s verse, as [the Mishnah] teaches: "If so, why is it stated: 'Every dedicated item,' etc.?"

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:3:1.hebrew: שהקדיש שדה חרמו - שדה שהחרים ישראל והגיע לחלק כהן שדה; שלא יאמר: הואיל וכשיגיע יובל, אם לא אפדנה אני מיד גזבר ויגאלנה אחר, תתחלק לכהנים ביובל כדין מקדיש שדה אחוזה — דהא שדה חרם לגבי כהן אחוזה היא, כדכתיב "כשדה החרם לכהן תהיה אחוזתו" — ועכשיו שאני מוחזק בה, תהא שלי; שהרי דין הוא: בשל אחרים אני זוכה — אם היה ישראל מקדיש שדה אחוזתו, כשיגיע יובל תתחלק לי — בשל עצמי לא כל שכן:
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:3:1.english: Who consecrated his dedicated field - [This refers to] a field that an Israelite dedicated and that fell to the portion of a priest. [The verse teaches] that he should not say: "Since when the Jubilee arrives, if I do not redeem it from the Temple treasurer and another [person] redeems it, it will be divided among the priests at the Jubilee in accordance with the law of one who consecrates an ancestral field — for a dedicated field is [considered] an ancestral field with respect to a priest, as it is written, 'As a field dedicated; its possession shall be to the priest' — and now, since I am in possession of it, it should be mine; for this is a logical inference: I acquire [a share] in the property of others — [namely,] if an Israelite had consecrated his ancestral field, when the Jubilee arrives it would be divided to me — in my own [property], all the more so!"

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:4:1.english: The verse states, “As a field dedicated,” etc. - for this verse is written regarding one who consecrates an ancestral field:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:5:1.hebrew: מה למדנו משדה החרם - על שדה אחוזה כו', מה שדה אחוזה שהקדיש ישראל וגאלה אחד מן הכהנים — תצא מידו ביובל ותתחלק לכל בני המשמר, כדאמר בפירקין דלעיל: "אחוזתו שלו ואין זו שלו" — אף שדה חרמו כו':
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:5:1.english: What have we learned from a dedicated field - [i.e.,] regarding an ancestral field, etc.? Just as an ancestral field that an Israelite consecrated and one of the priests redeemed leaves his possession at the Jubilee and is divided among all the members of the [priestly] watch — as it says in the previous chapter: "His ancestral [field] is his, and this [one] is not his" — so too his dedicated field, etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:8:1.hebrew: סבר לה כרבי ישמעאל - דמפיק לה במתניתין מ"יקדיש" ו"אל תקדיש":
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:8:1.english: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael - who derives it in the Mishnah [below] from [the verses] "he shall consecrate" and "do not consecrate":

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:9:1.hebrew: הלכה כר' יהודה בן בתירא - דסתם חרמים לבדק הבית:
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:9:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira - that unspecified dedications [are] for Temple maintenance:

Rashi on Arakhin 29a:9:2.hebrew: ברייתא איפכא תניא - דרבנן אמרי לבדק הבית, ורבי יהודה לכהנים:
Rashi on Arakhin 29a:9:2.english: A baraita is taught [in the] opposite [manner] - That the Rabbis say [unspecified dedications go] to Temple maintenance, and Rabbi Yehuda [ben Beteira says they go] to the priests:

Tosafot on Arakhin 29a:11:1.hebrew: שקול ד' זוזי ואחיל עלייהו ושדינהו בנהרא ולישתרי לך - ואם תאמר, והא אמר בפרק קמא דע"ז (דף יג. ושם): אין מקדישין ואין מחרימין ואין מעריכין בזמן הזה, ואם הקדיש והחרים והעריך — בהמה תעקר, פירות וכלים ירקבו; והכא בזמן הזה איירי, כדמסיק הכא, ואמאי לא אמרי' ירקבו? וצ"ל דדוקא במטלטלין קאמר דירקבו, דלא אתי בהו לידי תקלה אם ממתינים עד שירקבו; והכא במקרקעי איירי, דאם ימתין (לאו) אתי לידי תקלה. והכי נמי איתא בסמוך, דאמר: והא מעשה דפומבדיתא מקרקעי היה:
Tosafot on Arakhin 29a:11:1.english: Take four zuzim and desacralize [the property] onto them, and throw them into the river, and it will be permitted to you - And if you ask: Behold, it says in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (13a and there): One does not consecrate, nor dedicate, nor take a valuation vow nowadays, and if one consecrated, dedicated, or took a valuation vow — an animal should be destroyed, [and] produce and vessels should rot; and here [the Gemara] is dealing with nowadays, as it concludes here, so why do we not say "they should rot"? One must say that it only said "they should rot" with regard to movable property, for one will not come to a stumbling block with them if they wait until they rot; whereas here it is dealing with real estate, where if one waits, one will come to a stumbling block. And so too it is stated shortly below, where [the Gemara] says: "Wasn't the incident of Pumbedita [involving] real estate?":

Tosafot on Arakhin 29a:21:1.hebrew: הקדש עלוי - פי': להעלותו בדמים, ליתן טובת הנאה לכהן:
Tosafot on Arakhin 29a:21:1.english: Consecration of value - Meaning: to assess its monetary value [for the right] to give the benefit of discretion to a priest:
